title: Implementing Bell causality in Quantum Sequential Growth
locator: Sec. 3.1, especially Lemma 3.1; Secs. 3.2–3.5 for QBC variants; Sec. 4 Discussion, paragraph beginning ‘Apart from operator ordering ambiguities’
assumptions: Quantum sequential growth with operator-valued transitions; non-singular dynamics for the central results; several explicitly selected operator orderings for quantum Bell causality. The norm-only GC/path-phase paragraph is a proposed alternative, not the main derived framework.
conclusion: The paper expressly notes that GC could require only equality of the quantum vector-measure norm, allowing path-dependent phases, and that phases could also enter QBC; it says these options rapidly become complex and leaves further exploration open. Under stated functional assumptions, Lemma 3.1 reconstructs transition operators from gregarious operators.
proof_status: Relevant full-text passages read; no full algebraic proof audit or code audit.
relevance: Strongest direct anticipation of the conceptual norm-only phase option. The sidecar may be a restricted scalar realization of the option the authors describe.
limits: Does not establish in the inspected passages the exact scalar ratio-BC classification, shape-dependent q(C) seed, or percolation-reference L1 completion. Operator-valued QBC is a different domain; its future-work statement is not evidence of global priority.

title: A Criterion for Covariance in Complex Sequential Growth Models
locator: Sec. 3.1 Theorem 3.1 and Claims 3.2–3.3; Sec. 3.2 Corollary 3.6; Sec. 3.3 Claims 3.8–3.9 and Eqs. (54)–(62)
assumptions: Complex Sequential Growth in the standard cardinality-coupling form, with the vector measure on labelled histories; bounded variation criteria govern extension to the generated sigma algebra and hence measurability of covariant events.
conclusion: Summability of maximal row excess is sufficient for bounded variation; divergence of minimal row excess rules it out. The authors give nontrivial non-real extendible families with asymptotically colinear late couplings, alongside nonextendible examples.
proof_status: Full text read for cited sections and displayed derivations/examples; appendix and all dependencies not newly audited; no code audit.
relevance: Defeats novelty claims for summable-variation extension methods and complex extendible causal-set growth in general; its criteria frame the sidecar's percolation-tail completion as an application.
limits: Standard cardinality-coupling CSG and full vector-measure extension setting; no exact match found in the inspected passages for the sidecar's shape-dependent early q(C), norm-only cylinder condition, or finite perturbation of a real-percolation reference.
